findings.claim: observed — the template's scanner ports core's open-substitution arm but not core's `(`-group / `)`-paren-stack arms, so a `#` after `(` or after an operator `)` is read as text; a `<<word` in that text opens a heredoc whose unterminated body blanks every later line, and a merge bash DOES run goes unjudged (third divergence of the same fail-open class; core's rule is stated verbatim at packages/core/src/transport-shield.ts:213-219 and implemented at :367-377)
findings.counterexample:
(true)#<<note
gh pr merge 5 · (#<<note
gh pr merge 5
) · (true; echo a)#<<note
gh pr merge 5 — bash 5.3.15 executes the merge line in all three; the committed wrapper never spawns the CLI and exits 0

findings.claim: observed — the template's bare heredoc-delimiter class /[A-Za-z0-9_.\-\/]/ is narrower than core's HEREDOC_AT bare word [^\s'"\\<>()|&;]+ (packages/core/src/transport-shield.ts:210-211), so a delimiter containing any other character is parsed as a PREFIX, the real terminator line never matches, and the body scan blanks to end of input — falsifying the shipped comment at init-templates.ts:1521-1524 that the blanker models bare delimiters 'the shape core's transport-shield scanner uses'
findings.counterexample:
cat <<E:F
body
E:F
gh pr merge 5 (also E*F, E+F, E=F, E,F, E@F, E!F, EOF~) — bash terminates the body at the delimiter and runs the merge; the wrapper never spawns
